text:
incidents-bot: ALERT 1749123456 — High latency detected on dedicated pool 'apex-prod-1'. p99 token latency > 800ms, error rate ~0.8%. Paging oncall @Ryan.
Ryan: ACK. Joining bridge :phone:
Ana: Jumping into metrics and logs. I see sustained backend compute spikes tied to tenant apex-inc-42. GPU queue depth up, kernel wait times spiking.
Sam: Is this noisy-tenant activity? Apex has this pool as a dedicated enterprise tenant — we should avoid blunt eviction. Options: isolate tenant traffic, soft-throttle, or route that tenant to a faster/fallback model.
Maya: From CS/accounting: what is the customer-level impact here? Apex team is sensitive to any evictions. Need exact wording for support comms.
Lucas: Customer reported intermittent errors and slow responses for some calls. They want ETA.
Ryan: Mitigation plan: 1) enable per-tenant soft throttle for apex-inc-42, 2) set model fallback to rwd-fast-q4f16 for that tenant, 3) enable prefix KV caching for the tenant session. Rolling now.
Ana: Commands I'm running: `redwoodctl pools tenant-throttle --pool apex-prod-1 --tenant apex-inc-42 --rate 0.6 --soft` then `redwoodctl routes set-fallback --tenant apex-inc-42 --model rwd-fast-q4f16`
incidents-bot: Action logged: mitigation steps applied by Ryan at 1749123490. Metrics will stabilize in ~2 minutes.
Sam: Observing queue length drop. p95 latency down to ~180ms, p99 ~300ms. Looks like mitigation is effective. Continue monitoring for regressions.
Maya: Update sent to customer: 'We observed a noisy workload inside your dedicated pool; we applied targeted throttling and a fallback model for the noisy tenant. Performance should be restored. We're preparing an exec summary and a post-incident RCA and will follow up on any credits.'
Lucas: Customer is asking about credits/SLA remedies. Proposal from CS: offer pro-rated credit for the interval where p99 > 500ms plus proactive offer to host heavy batch jobs in a separate reserved pool. Thoughts?
Sam: Sounds reasonable. Final credit calc needs Finance sign-off. Also recommend runtime hardening: tenant-level rate limit enforcement and autoscaling headroom adjustments to avoid headroom exhaustion.
Ryan: Post-incident owners: RCA draft (Ana), Exec brief + customer comms (Maya + Lucas), Credit proposal (Ryan -> Finance), Runtime prevention plan (Sam). I'll create GH issue and tag owners.
Ana: I'll assemble RCA timeline. Preliminary root cause: a config rollout (PR#482) unintentionally relaxed rate-limit checks for internal batch jobs, allowing apex-inc-42 to burst beyond expected throughput. Will include logs + trace IDs.
incidents-bot: Incident status updated to MITIGATED at 1749123580. Please update follow-up items.
Sam: Assigning owners/ETAs: RCA (Ana) EOD draft, Exec brief (Maya) draft for review by EOD, Credit calc (Ryan) preliminary number tomorrow AM, Runtime hardening (Sam) plan by EOD.
Maya: I'll draft the exec summary now — concise timeline, mitigation applied, proposed customer-facing wording, and next steps. Will post here for review.
Lucas: I'll be on standby to adapt the customer note once Maya's draft is posted.
Ryan: :thumbsup: I'll keep bridge open for 10 more minutes and close if metrics remain stable.
Ana: RCA draft posted: https://redwood.internal/r/rca/1749123456. Key findings: feature flag allowed rate-limit bypass; fix = rollback + unit tests + gating; mitigation = tenant soft-throttle + fallback model.
Sam: Applied runtime config changes: `pool.apex-prod-1.autoscale.min=2` and `pool.apex-prod-1.headroom_pct=30` to increase headroom and reduce queue spikes.
Maya: Exec brief shared with account execs; they requested an initial credit estimate. We'll align with Finance tomorrow.
incidents-bot: Thread marked CLOSED at 1749123800 — follow-ups assigned (RCA, exec brief, credit calc, runtime hardening).
